lines: Car tires used to be white.
Natural rubber is actually a milky white color.
But those first white tires wore out really fast.
Some barely lasted a few thousand miles.
Then tire makers started mixing in a black powder.
It's called carbon black. Basically super fine soot.
It makes the rubber way stronger,
and blocks the sunlight that cracks rubber.
Suddenly, tires lasted many times longer.
That's why every tire you see today is black.
Just a thin white layer on the side.
